analysis.title: IR+M Fixed Income Market Update, October 2026
key_insights: The Fed held the federal funds target range at 3.75-4.00% in October after a rate hike in September. Several officials said further hikes may be needed to bring inflation back toward target.

Treasury yields fell sharply in October. The 10-year yield dropped 36bps to 4.93% and the 30-year dropped 32bps to 5.31%. Softer employment data, strong auction demand and a late-month flight to quality drove the move.
September payrolls rose 29k against an expected 90k, and the unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. October's PMI Composite stayed expansionary at 57.6.
A $39 billion 10-year Treasury auction awarded at 5.30%, below the prevailing yield at the time. Higher yields drew buyers back to the long end and eased concerns about demand for government debt.

Credit spreads widened with softer risk sentiment. IG spreads rose from 80bps to 90bps and HY spreads rose from 311bps to 340bps. IG all-in yields fell from 6.04% to 5.79% and HY yields eased from 8.35% to 8.31%.
IG corporate issuance was about $123 billion in October. Year-to-date issuance is $1.8 trillion, on pace to beat the 2020 annual record, with AI-related capital needs adding to borrowing.
HY issuance was about $15 billion, the slowest month since spring, as higher funding costs weighed on lower-rated borrowers.
Agency MBS outperformed most spread sectors. Lower Treasury yields and lower rate volatility tightened MBS spreads from 43bps to 34bps.

Municipal bonds had their strongest October in more than four decades, with the Bloomberg Municipal Bond Index up about 3.9%. The 2-year muni/Treasury ratio fell from 73% to 61% and the 30-year ratio edged down from 93% to 92%.
The market stayed focused on persistent inflation, fiscal sustainability and the path of monetary policy. US deficit and financing concerns kept long-end Treasury supply and demand in focus.
